To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the implementation of filters with best-available technology to gasoline direct injection (GDI) engines can lower nanoparticle and genotoxic PAH emissions substantially.
the implementation of best-available GPF technology to GDI vehicles is essential to avoid store-and-releases of nanoparticles and genotoxic PAH.
GDI vehicle exhausts are a major source of nanoparticles and genotoxic PAH emissions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of novel technologies to reduce the emissions of ultrafine particles and associated genotoxic PAH compounds from GDI vehicles.
the development of GPFs for GDI vehicles to lower emissions of nanoparticles and genotoxic PAH emissions to the lowest possible level.
the development of GPFs for the mitigation of the health effects of GDI exhaust emissions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GPFs can reduce the genotoxic potential of GDI vehicle exhausts, but the current state-of-the-art GPFs are not yet able to reduce the emissions of genotoxic PAHS and PN to levels below the current EU emission limits.
the implementation of filters is required to avoid the expected deterioration of the air quality in Europe.
GPFs can be an important tool to reduce the emissions of nanoparticles and genotoxic PAH from GDI vehicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination of GPF-1 and an oxidation catalyst (GPF-1+CAT) would lower particle emissions by 98% and genotoxic PAH emissions by 90% and thus would be the best available technology for GDI vehicles.

a combination of the most effective GPF-1 and a diesel particulate filter (DPF) in a series configuration would lower PN 4.5 × 104-fold to 0.01 × 1011/km and 5-fold for genotoxic PAH emissions to 9 ng TEQ/km.
GPFs with high filtration efficiency and catalytic activity should be implemented to GDI vehicles to reduce the health risk to the population, especially in urban areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
particle filtration and reduction of the associated genotoxic PAH emissions is possible, but requires best available technology.
the implementation of GPFs is an important step in the development of cleaner and more sustainable GDI vehicles.
GPFs are an important tool to mitigate the impact of GDI vehicles on urban air quality.
